data.title: Modal
data.tagline: Pause the page for one focused decision or task
data.description: A modal appears above the page when the user must review or complete a focused task before continuing. It needs a clear title, a safe way to close, sensible keyboard focus, and buttons that state the result. Long or complex work is usually better on its own page.

use: Choose one item without losing the current page
avoid: Open a modal for ordinary navigation
Place a long multi-step workflow inside a small box
Stack one modal on top of another
Remove every safe way to close it

lessonPractice.title: Editing a billing address has several fields but should not leave the order page. When does a Modal fit?

options.label: Use a Modal for this short, focused edit with clear save and close
options.feedback: Correct. A separate, brief task needing focus fits a modal; long or multi-step work belongs on a full page.

options.label: Put every explanatory line in a Modal so it is always seen
options.feedback: Frequent interruption adds burden; simple guidance does not need a modal layer.

options.label: Put primary site navigation in a Modal
options.feedback: Navigation should remain predictable and returnable, not trap site paths in a dialog.

data.agentPrompt: Put order-page address editing in a Modal. On open, move focus to its title or first field; provide Save and Close, then return focus to the trigger on close. Test saving once and closing with Esc once, confirming background actions cannot fire and focus returns correctly.
